_note: INFORMATION TEXTS for the English literacy year (Daily Teaching System, Part 12.3; read by a US Grade 1 reading reviewer 2026-11-15 and corrected by every finding; read a second time after the corrections (four small wording points, applied)). The reading banks held stories only; the Common Core RI standards need texts that inform. Grade 1: about 60 to 75 words in two sections, each with a heading; two words in bold; a three-word glossary; one library picture with a caption. Every fact must be one a teacher can confirm; every question has one right answer that a sentence of the text gives (its 1-based number is `sentence`). `topic` = the main topic and two wrong choices (a detail of the text; a thing the text only mentions). `full` = the whole answer sentence of a question (it starts with `starter`); `lure` = a word of the text that is not in bold (a wrong choice of the bold-word question); `capChoices` = two wrong answers of the caption question; `picture2` = a second picture of something the text tells about, with a sample caption. `features` = find-it questions answered from a text feature, not from the running text. `headLure` = a heading the text does not have (the third choice of a heading question: a child may call the title the main heading). KINDERGARTEN (`k`; read by a US kindergarten reviewer 2026-11-15 and corrected by every finding, then read a second time and corrected again): four sentences in big print; every question is read aloud by the teacher and answered by circling one of three library pictures (`right`, `wrong`; `draw` = the question as it stands on the levels where the child draws); `topic` = the picture of the main topic and the pictures of the two key details; `details` = the numbers of the two sentences that are key details. Added 2026-11-15 for two more pages and read by a US kindergarten reviewer (every finding applied): the texts `oak-trees` and `rain` (`since`: the two first pages do not draw them, so their published pages stay what they are); `match` = the matching page of a text: the picture of each sentence, its own wording of a sentence where needed, and which pictures may be the missing one on the hard level; `change` = what comes first and what comes then in a text that tells a change, a picture that is no part of it, the two words, and its own wording of the text where needed. GRADE 2 (`g2`; read twice by a US Grade 2 reviewer 2026-11-15 and corrected by every finding): about 150 words in three parts (the pages 1-3 of a small book), each with a heading and one bold word; two pictures with captions; a four-word glossary; an index (word → page); `focus` = what each part is mostly about, `focusLure` = a focus no part has; `topic` = the main topic, a detail and a too-wide choice; `features` = six find-it questions (a caption question names its two wrong answers; the others take them from the text).
